chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bequeathed a third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and his maternal uncles, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the paternal uncles is two-thirds, and for the maternal uncles is one-third.'
ai.seo_question: How is a bequest distributed between paternal and maternal uncles according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s (peace be upon him) application of equitable distribution principles in inheritance law, distinguishing between paternal and maternal kinship lines. It highlights the scholarly tradition of allocating two-thirds to the paternal uncles and one-third to the maternal uncles, reflecting the nuanced jurisprudence (fiqh) regarding bequests outside of obligatory shares. This ruling serves as a practical example of how the Imams interpreted the flexibility of the one-third bequest limit in relation to specific familial relationships.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who bequeathed with a third of his wealth among his paternal uncles and his maternal uncles. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the paternal uncles is two thirds, and for the maternal uncles is a third’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who bequests one-third of his legacy to his paternal and maternal uncles. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The paternal uncle receive two-thirds and the maternal uncle receives one-third.’”
